_meta.note: Demo values for a hackathon tool, not medical advice. Each value cites its source; 'assumption' marks a value we chose where no primary source gives one.
_meta.status_rule: A reading is green inside 'green', orange inside 'orange' (outside green), red otherwise. Ranges are inclusive [min, max]; null = no bound.
_meta.flight_rule: temp: before applying thresholds, subtract the expected in-flight rise for the current day (drift.<location>.temp_rise_c, linear from day 0 to reached_at_day). A +1 °C rise alone stays green on long missions.
_meta.to_verify: Thresholds and study figures were written from memory during the hackathon: check against the sources before the final submission.
_meta.zones: heart, metabolism, brain, sleep, bones, skin, eyes, back, core (core = whole body: the silhouette outline glows, used for temperature)

sources.aha_bp: American Heart Association, Understanding Blood Pressure Readings (2017 ACC/AHA categories) - heart.org
sources.aha_hr: American Heart Association, All About Heart Rate (resting 60-100 bpm) - heart.org
sources.ada_glucose: American Diabetes Association, Standards of Care: Diagnosis (fasting 100-125 prediabetes, >=126 diabetes); hypoglycemia level 1 <70, level 2 <54 mg/dL
sources.temp_clinical: Usual clinical ranges: 36.1-37.2 °C normal, >=38.0 °C fever, <35 °C hypothermia
sources.stahn_2017: Stahn A.C. et al., Increased core body temperature in astronauts during long-duration space missions, Scientific Reports 7, 16180 (2017): about +1 °C at rest after ~2.5 months
sources.aasm_sleep: AASM / Sleep Research Society consensus: adults need 7 h or more per night (Watson et al., Sleep 2015)
sources.barger_2014: Barger L.K. et al., Prevalence of sleep deficiency and use of hypnotics in astronauts, Lancet Neurology 13(9) (2014): about 6 h/night on the ISS
sources.nasa_hrp_bone: NASA Human Research Program, Risks of Human Spaceflight: bone loss of about 1-1.5 % per month in weight-bearing bones in microgravity - nasa.gov/hrp/risks
sources.nasa_hrp_hazards: NASA Human Research Program, 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight - nasa.gov/hrp/hazards
sources.nasa_std_3001: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 Rev. B (2022): career effective dose limit 600 mSv
sources.nasa_iss_dose: NASA: ISS crew receive about 80-160 mSv over a 6-month mission (about 0.4-0.9 mSv/day)
sources.zeitlin_2013: Zeitlin C. et al., Measurements of energetic particle radiation in transit to Mars on the Mars Science Laboratory, Science 340 (2013): 1.84 mSv/day in cruise
sources.zhang_2020: Zhang S. et al., First measurements of the radiation dose on the lunar surface (Chang'e 4 LND), Science Advances 6(39) (2020): 1.369 mSv/day
sources.assumption: Chosen by the team for the demo, no primary source
sources.basner_2011: Basner M., Mollicone D., Dinges D.F., Validity and sensitivity of a brief psychomotor vigilance test (PVT-B), Acta Astronautica 69 (2011): 3-minute test, lapse = response > 355 ms
sources.nasa_reaction_self_test: NASA ISS experiment Reaction Self Test (Dinges, Basner): astronauts run a 3-minute PVT on a laptop or iPad to track fatigue - nasa.gov ISS research
sources.nasa_hrp_sans: NASA Human Research Program, Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS): optic disc edema, globe flattening, hyperopic shift on long missions - nasa.gov/hrp
sources.mader_2011: Mader T.H. et al., Optic disc edema, globe flattening, choroidal folds and hyperopic shifts in astronauts after long-duration space flight, Ophthalmology 118(10) (2011)
sources.kerstman_2012: Kerstman E.L. et al., Space adaptation back pain: a retrospective study, Aviation, Space and Environmental Medicine 83(1) (2012): about half of astronauts report back pain, mostly in the first days
sources.johnston_2010: Johnston S.L. et al., Risk of herniated nucleus pulposus among U.S. astronauts, Aviation, Space and Environmental Medicine 81(6) (2010): about 4x higher disc herniation risk after flight
sources.nrs_pain: Numeric pain rating scale 0-10: 1-3 mild, 4-6 moderate, 7-10 severe (common clinical cut-offs)

advice.orange: Rest 5 minutes and measure again. Note caffeine, exercise or stress.
advice.red: Measure again at rest. If it stays out of range, or with chest pain, dizziness or shortness of breath, contact the flight surgeon.

advice.orange: Measure again seated after 5 minutes of rest, twice, 1 minute apart. Watch salt and hydration.
advice.red: Above 140 (or below 85): measure again, then report to the flight surgeon. Above 180: contact the ground now.

advice.orange: Measure again after rest. Note it in the log.
advice.red: Measure again, then report to the flight surgeon. Above 120: contact the ground now.

advice.orange: Below 70: eat 15 g of fast sugar and measure again in 15 minutes. 100-125: check meals and exercise, measure again tomorrow fasting.
advice.red: Below 54: take sugar now and alert the crew. 126 or more: measure again fasting, then report to the flight surgeon.

temp.label: Body temperature
temp.space_note: Core temperature rises by about 1 °C at rest on long missions (stahn_2017): a mild rise alone is expected, look at the trend and symptoms.

advice.orange: Hydrate, measure again in 1 hour, note any symptoms.
advice.red: 38 °C or more: possible infection (the immune system changes in space). Isolate if possible and contact the flight surgeon.

sleep_h.label: Sleep last night
sleep_h.space_note: ISS crews sleep about 6 h on average (barger_2014). Sleep debt adds up over days.
sleep_h.trend_rule: Orange if the 7-day average is under 6.5 h, even when last night was green.

advice.orange: Protect the next sleep slot: dim the light 1 hour before, eye mask, no screen.
advice.red: Under 6 h several nights in a row lowers attention: avoid critical tasks if possible and tell the commander.

mood.label: Mood (self-rating)
mood.space_note: Isolation and confinement is one of the 5 hazards (nasa_hrp_hazards).
mood.trend_rule: Orange if the 7-day average drops by 1 point or more.

advice.orange: Plan a call with family, an exercise session or a crew activity.
advice.red: Talk to the flight psychologist at the next private conference. You are not alone.

bone_loss_pct.label: Bone density lost since launch
bone_loss_pct.space_note: About 1-1.5 % lost per month in microgravity (nasa_hrp_bone). Thresholds are a demo choice.

advice.orange: Keep the daily resistance exercise (2 h/day on the ISS), calcium and vitamin D.
advice.red: Report to the flight surgeon: increase resistance exercise, avoid high-impact tasks.

radiation_msv.label: Cumulative radiation dose
radiation_msv.space_note: Thresholds = 50 % and 80 % of the 600 mSv career limit (nasa_std_3001); orange and red are a demo choice.

advice.orange: Spend sleep time in the most shielded area. Check upcoming solar activity.
advice.red: Close to the career limit: the ground decides on EVAs and the mission plan.

reaction_time_ms.label: Reaction time (3-min vigilance test)
reaction_time_ms.space_note: Astronauts already run this test on the ISS (nasa_reaction_self_test). Mean above 355 ms = the lapse threshold. Green limit 300 ms is a demo choice.
reaction_time_ms.input_hint: Tap as soon as a counter appears, random delay 2-10 s, for 3 minutes; value = mean response time.

advice.orange: Fatigue sign: check last nights' sleep, take a break before a precise task.
advice.red: Slowed reflexes: avoid robotic arm, EVA or other critical tasks until rested, tell the commander.

vision_lines_lost.label: Near vision change (lines lost on the eye chart vs before launch)
vision_lines_lost.space_note: SANS: fluid shifts toward the head can change the eye on long missions (mader_2011). Thresholds are a demo choice.

advice.orange: Do the test again tomorrow in the same light; note headaches.
advice.red: Report to the flight surgeon: an eye ultrasound or OCT check may be planned.

back_pain.label: Back pain (0-10)
back_pain.space_note: The spine lengthens in microgravity; about half of astronauts get back pain in the first days (kerstman_2012), and disc herniation risk is higher after return (johnston_2010).

advice.orange: Knees-to-chest position, gentle stretching, note it in the log.
advice.red: Severe or with numbness in the legs: contact the flight surgeon.

drift._note: Inputs for simulate(location, days). Rates per day unless stated. noise = standard deviation of the daily random part.

back_pain.note: Peak in the first week, then mostly resolves.

reaction_time_ms.note: Linked to the 7-day sleep average below 7 h.

vision_lines_lost.note: SANS on part of the crew only (nasa_hrp_sans).

sleep_h_mean.note: ISS value (barger_2014), more noise for distance and isolation.

mood_drift_per_month.note: Isolation hazard, no ground contact in real time.
